title: CSS Modules
description: Scope CSS automatically with CSS Modules, compose classes, and type your styles in TypeScript.

data.text: CSS Modules compile every class name into a unique, hashed identifier at build time. Styles stay plain CSS (so there is no runtime cost), but collisions between components become impossible.

data.caption: src/components/Button.module.css
src/components/Button.tsx

data.text: `composes` pulls declarations from another local class without duplicating CSS. Every name is local by default; wrap selectors in `:global(...)` when you genuinely need a global hook (for example a third-party widget).

data.title: Expose a single global class and add types
CSS Modules do not add cascade awareness
data.text: Two modules can still fight over a shared global (for example `body`) or over specificity inside a composed class. Keep modules component-sized and style layout in a parent.

terms.definition: A .module.css file whose class names are hashed and exported as a JavaScript object.
A CSS Modules directive that reuses declarations from another local class.
An escape hatch that keeps a selector unscoped.
A .d.ts file describing the shape of the imported class map for TypeScript.

data.title: Key takeaways
points: CSS Modules scope class names at build time with zero runtime cost.
composes reuses declarations without duplicating CSS.
Use :global only for real global hooks such as body or a vendor widget.
Add a *.module.css declaration file when TypeScript cannot find the types.
data.takeaway: CSS Modules are the pragmatic middle ground between plain CSS and CSS-in-JS.
